title: NATO Releases Quantum Technology Roadmap
source_used: The Quantum Insider (30 Sep 2026); DSEI Gateway page rate-limited (HTTP 429)
key_facts: NATO's new Quantum Technology Roadmap sets dates for testing quantum technology in military use and for defending against quantum threats
QUESTOR sea trials of quantum sensors in 2026 and 2027, aimed at navigation and timing where satellite signals are unavailable
First military pilot evaluation report in the first quarter of 2027
Communications pilot linking NATO headquarters in Brussels and Mons, Belgium, by end of 2027
Design concept for an allied quantum computing access network in the fourth quarter of 2027, a design milestone not a working network
Plan includes adopting post-quantum cryptography standards
NATO says later stages depend on technical progress and early trial results; roadmap builds on the strategy adopted in November 2023
quote_evidence: The alliance's new Quantum Technology Roadmap calls for sea trials of quantum sensors in 2026 and 2027.
The document stops short of promising broad military deployment on a fixed schedule.
why_it_matters_hint: A schedule of trials and security tasks, not a promise of deployed quantum weapons or networks.
notes: Older news re-posted: The Quantum Insider covered the roadmap on 30 Sep 2026; DSEI Gateway page blocked.
